exposure: Two different doses of hyperbaric intrathecal bupivacaine with fentanyl (specifically, 10 mg bupivacaine with 25 mcg fentanyl vs. a comparatively higher dose)
outcome: Onset and duration of sensory block
Onset and duration of motor block
Intraoperative visceral and somatic pain (aim to avoid)
cohort: The study included 100 consenting pregnant mothers of ASA II status who underwent emergency lower uterine caesarian section.
finding: The study concludes that using 10 mg of hyperbaric bupivacaine with 25 mcg of fentanyl in pregnant mothers for subarachnoid block in emergency LUCS provides better perioperative outcomes, including a longer duration of analgesia, a shorter time for onset of sensory and motor block, a longer duration of sensory and motor block, a longer duration of anaesthesia, and no significant changes in hemodynamic status.
mod_finding: The study found that using 10 mg of hyperbaric bupivacaine with 25 mcg of fentanyl provides better perioperative outcomes for pregnant mothers undergoing emergency lower uterine caesarean section.
